oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — High error rate detected on embeddings->reranker pipeline (service: embeddings-batch -> reranker-queue). Paging oncall. incident_id=INC-2027-045. @dmitri you're oncall

Dmitri: taking this. seeing spike ~03:10 UTC, 5xxs from reranker service. Paging + creating thread for mitigation. Anyone with recent deploys to embedding or reranker?

Cassie: quick numbers: error rate ~18% over last 6m, p95 latency up, ~420 requests failed. Affected customers: internal QA job + 2 prod customers using batch embed->rerank. Errors start at 03:09:43 UTC.

Maya: looking at logs — reranker returns 500s with InvalidVectorSize in stacktrace. Posting sample:

```
2027-02-12T03:09:47Z ERROR reranker.request InvalidVectorSize: expected dim=1536, got dim=1024
  at /srv/reranker/handler.py:87
  at process_batch (/srv/reranker/batch.py:210)
  payload_id: 0f4a2c
```

Sahil: interesting — last night we rolled a conversion script for the new compact embedder quantization. That should keep dimensionality the same, but maybe a variant got swapped.

Dmitri: hypothesis table in-thread so we don't scatter notes. H1: embedder conversion produced 1024-d vectors instead of 1536 (bad variant). H2: batch API serializes/truncates vectors under certain batch sizes. H3: reranker model expectation changed via deploy (unlikely, no reranker deploys in last 24h).

Cassie: I pulled an example request from the batch queue — embedding payload shows length 1024 consistently for some batches. Putting sanitized payload snippet:

```
{ "request_id": "0f4a2c", "embeddings": [ [0.001, -0.003, ... /* 1024 floats */ ] ], "meta": {"model": "redwood-embed-compact-v1"} }
```

Alex: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) add an input dimension guard at reranker (reject with 4xx instead of 500), 2) route batch traffic that contains suspect model tag to legacy reranker variant that tolerates 1024, or 3) temporarily disable the new encoder conversion in the batch pipeline. Which is fastest?

Sahil: (1) is quick but still surfaces errors to customers. (2) requires routing change, doable via routing-service flag. (3) is rollback of conversion — would fix source but takes longer to validate. My vote: route suspect traffic to fallback and also add guard in reranker to avoid 500s.

Dmitri: agreed. @alex can you patch routing-policy to send requests with meta.model=="redwood-embed-compact-v1" to reranker-legacy? Alex, can you also post the curl you used?

Alex: pushing routing change now. command:

```
# add temporary rule to routing-service
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/rules -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTING_TOKEN" -d '{"match": {"meta.model": "redwood-embed-compact-v1"}, "route": "reranker-legacy"}'
```

Alex: rule applied and propagated to edge nodes (~30s). I also throttled the embeddings-batch producer for suspect model to reduce error volume.

Opsbot: ROUTE UPDATE successful: rule_id=rr-2027-301 applied to 12 edge nodes.

Cassie: after routing change error rate dropped to ~1.5% in last 4m. p95 latency returned to baseline. Customers impacted: started recovering. Notifying customer success.

Evan: I'll open CS notifications and draft a short customer note: "we detected issue affecting some batch embedding jobs; we've applied a mitigation and are investigating root cause; will follow up with RCA."

Maya: digging deeper into embedding conversion job logs. I found a commit that changed the quantization config and a conversion run at 01:20 UTC that produced artifacts with an internal metadata tag that omitted dim field. Looks suspicious.

Cassie: posting timeline so far:
- 01:20 UTC: convert-embed job ran (suspect)
- 03:09:43 UTC: first 500s in reranker observed
- 03:10:15 UTC: oncall-bot page sent
- 03:12:00 UTC: routing rule applied to divert suspect model -> reranker-legacy
- 03:16:00 UTC: error rate down to baseline

Dmitri: running quick check: list of artifacts from conversion job shows mixed dims: some artifacts = 1536, some = 1024. Looks like artifact tagging logic failed and the batch job picked the wrong artifact for some shards.

Sahil: that explains it. Root cause hypothesis updated: conversion job produced mixed-dimension artifacts due to a race in artifact registry; batch builder later picked artifact with 1024 dims for subset of shards.

Maya: next immediate steps (I've created short task list):
- Create automated validation in convert-embed pipeline to assert dim==1536 for all artifacts (task: ENG-embed-1542)
- Add schema validation at embeddings-batch API to reject invalid dims (ENG-api-1729)
- Add canary check in routing to detect sudden dimension mismatch and auto-divert (ENG-runtime-1601)
- Post-incident: full RCA doc and postmortem (PMR-2027-045)

Dmitri: handoff to night shift @maya. I'll add a short handoff summary and assign follow-ups.

Dmitri: Handoff summary: mitigation applied (routing rule), error rate reduced, customers notified, pursuing conversion pipeline fix. Assigned tickets: ENG-embed-1542 (high), ENG-api-1729 (medium), ENG-runtime-1601 (low).

Maya: taking over for night. Will monitor for any replays or additional affected batches, and start on validation for conversion job. If routing reverts, I'll rollback and re-divert.

Cassie: recording minimal customer impact: some batch jobs retried automatically by clients; 2 customers saw partial failures in specific batches — CS is coordinating follow-up.

Dmitri: thanks all. we'll convert this thread into a full postmortem doc and link it from incident tracking. If anyone has additional logs or sample payloads, paste them here. :thumbsup:

Evan: CS note sent to impacted contacts. Will attach log snippets from customers if they share.

Cassie: adding note to incident tracking: probable root cause = mixed-dimension artifacts from conversion job -> batch picked wrong shard artifact -> reranker failed with InvalidVectorSize.

Maya: quick command I ran to find differing dims across artifacts:
```
python tools/check_artifacts.py --prefix s3://embedder/2027-02-12/ --expected-dim 1536
# found: 12/420 artifacts dim=1024
```

Dmitri: good work. We'll add automated gating to avoid repeat. Closing active mitigation as resolved; leaving RCA work items open.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied and stable. Closing active page. incident_id=INC-2027-045.
